subject: DPA: controller/processor mapping, logging granularity & residency — post-demo follow-up
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medsys.com>, contracts@medsys.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: DPA clarifications re: controller roles, subprocessors, and logging

Hi Lena / MedSys team —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Wanted to capture the open privacy / DPA items we discussed and clarify next steps from our side so you have everything for legal/security review. TL;DR: we can support EU residency for model hosting, provide SOC 2 evidence, and will send a current subprocessor list + sample logs. A few clarifying questions below so we can produce the exact artifacts you need.

Call recap & asks
1) Controller vs. Processor: You asked us to confirm Redwood's role for the primary integration (API-driven inference where MedSys supplies patient identifiers in prompts). Please confirm whether MedSys prefers Redwood to be explicitly listed as Processor with MedSys as Controller in the DPA. We will also outline any limited controller-like activities (e.g., metadata retention for billing) in a mapping doc.

2) Subprocessors: You requested the full list of subprocessors + notification process. We'll attach our current subprocessor CSV and describe our 30-day notify window for critical changes. Please confirm if MedSys needs contractual subprocessor flow-downs beyond our standard DPA.

3) Breach notice timing: You asked about SLA for breach notification. Our standard is to notify customers within 24 hours of confirming an incident affecting customer data; if you need a different threshold (e.g., 48 hours) for contract language, call that out.

4) Logging & retention: Clarify the granularity you need in logs (per-request headers, redacted prompt/response samples, token-level timing). Our default audit retention is 90 days for request metadata; we can offer extended retention on Dedicated or Private deployments.

5) Data residency: We can pin model hosting to EU or US regions for production. Confirm which region(s) MedSys wants specified in the DPA.

Attachments I'm sending with this message: redwood_dpa_summary_v1.pdf (summary of our standard addendum), and a blank mapping template. If you prefer, Marissa (cc'd) can create a controller/processor mapping draft for MedSys to review.

Next steps
- Please confirm which artifacts you want first (subprocessor list, SOC2, controller mapping, sample logs).
- If helpful, suggest 30 minutes for an internal security call next week and we can invite our Security/Privacy SME (Marissa).

Thanks — I think we're in good shape to get a DPA draft over once we confirm the mapping and residency.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few follow-ups from our side:

- MedSys expects to be Controller; yes, please list Redwood explicitly as Processor. That said, we need the mapping doc that shows any exceptions (billing metadata, aggregated metrics).

- Please send the current subprocessor roster and confirm your notification process; our procurement team often asks for proof of flow-down language.

- Breach notice: we prefer 24 hours for material incidents. Can you confirm whether Redwood's incident response timeline is contractual or operational?

- Logs: we need request-level metadata (timestamp, request id, worker node id), and redacted prompt/response samples for periodic audits. If you have a sample audit log export, that would help our security review. Also confirm retention options (90 days default; specify costs for 1y).

- Residency: For PHI use we need EU residency for initial pilot; confirm you can pin EU-only for production and what the migration path looks like.

If Marissa can lead the artifact delivery that'd be great — our contracts team will kick off review once we receive the SOC 2 and subprocessor CSV.

Lena Ortiz
Head of Security Engineering, MedSys

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@medsys.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: DPA clarifications re: controller roles, subprocessors, and logging

Hi Lena —

Copying answers inline and attaching the artifacts you requested. Short version up front: Redwood signs as Processor; we will provide a controller/processor mapping doc, current subprocessor list, SOC 2 report, and a small sample of redacted audit logs. We support EU-residency for production and can offer 90 days default retention with an option to purchase extended retention (1 year) — I list pricing guidance after the attachments section.

Quoted from your email: "MedSys expects to be Controller; yes, please list Redwood explicitly as Processor."
- Confirmed: we will produce a DPA with MedSys as Controller and Redwood as Processor. The attached mapping (dpa-controller-processor-mapping.docx) calls out exceptions (billing metadata retained for 30 days in aggregated form; no prompts are retained in plaintext by default).

"Please send the current subprocessor roster and confirm your notification process; our procurement team often asks for proof of flow-down language."
- Attached: subprocessor_list_20260314.csv (columns: name, purpose, country, contract_version). Our process: we notify customers within 30 days for non-critical additions; for critical infra changes that materially affect data handling we escalate and notify within 5 business days. Flow-down language: standard in our DPA (see section 6.3). If you need dedicated flow-down clauses, we can propose language for procurement.

"Breach notice: we prefer 24 hours for material incidents. Can you confirm whether Redwood's incident response timeline is contractual or operational?"
- We operationally target 24 hours for initial notification of confirmed incidents affecting customer data. We are open to contractually committing to 24 hours for material incidents; legal typically requires standard carve-outs (investigative period, false positives). We can draft proposed liability/notice language for your counsel.

"Logs: we need request-level metadata (timestamp, request id, worker node id), and redacted prompt/response samples for periodic audits. If you have a sample audit log export, that would help our security review. Also confirm retention options (90 days default; specify costs for 1y)."
- Attached: audit_logs_sample.txt (redacted). It includes request_id, timestamp (UTC), model variant, region tag, and worker_id (hashed). We do not include full prompt text in audit logs by default; we can provide redacted prompt/response snapshots for compliance audits under NDA.
- Retention: default metadata retention is 90 days. Extended retention (1 year) is available on Redwood Dedicated/Private or as an add-on for Hosted: ballpark +20% monthly for storage and retrieval costs — we will provide exact pricing in the procurement packet.

"Residency: For PHI use we need EU residency for initial pilot; confirm you can pin EU-only for production and what the migration path looks like."
- We can pin workloads to EU-only production regions (Redwood Dedicated in eu-west-1 or Private deployment inside your VPC). Migration path: pilot in EU region -> we finalize resource reservation -> production capacity reserved (2–4 week lead time for dedicated GPU pools). For stricter regulatory needs we recommend Private deployment.

Next steps / proposed artifacts
- Attached: subprocessor_list_20260314.csv, SOC2_report_redwood_2025.pdf, dpa-controller-processor-mapping.docx, audit_logs_sample.txt.
- Action: Karthik, can you propose 30 minutes with MedSys security + our Privacy SME to walk through the mapping and procurement asks? I propose Tue Mar 16 10:00 AM PT (link below).

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/view/67890
Calendar: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=mock-evt-20260316-1000-PT

If you want the SOC2 attestation under NDA-only conditions, we can put that in place quickly and send a curtain-peeled version for procurement review.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
